newsitem.title: GERMANY: DG Bank says to pay dividend for 1996.
newsitem.headline: DG Bank says to pay dividend for 1996.

text.p: German co-operative banking group Deutsche Genossenschaftsbank (DG Bank) said on Wednesday it planned to pay a dividend once again for 1996.
"We are delighted to continue the payout," board member Berthold Eichwald told a news conference.
Eichwald declined to specify how high the dividend would be.

DG Bank had originally threatened not to pay a dividend because three of its shareholders, regional clearing banks GZB, SGZ and WGZ, had blocked its plans for a 150 million mark nominal capital increase.
Eichwald said the banks had been in talks on the issue for several weeks and were nearer an agreement.
